1: Mosiah opens with "Yea, even doth not Isaiah say:" before the verse. That line is Abinadi introducing the quotation, not part of Isaiah's text. Mosiah also joins the two questions with a comma where KJV has a question mark after "report."
2: Mosiah reads "out of dry ground" where KJV reads "out of a dry ground." Punctuation also differs (a semicolon for a colon, and no comma after "see him").
3: Only punctuation differs: Mosiah has a semicolon where KJV has a colon after "grief."
4: Mosiah reads "he has borne our griefs" where KJV reads "he hath borne our griefs." Punctuation also differs (a semicolon for a colon).
5: Only punctuation differs: Mosiah has a semicolon where KJV has a colon after "iniquities."
6: Mosiah reads "the iniquities of us all" where KJV reads "the iniquity of us all." The Hebrew עֲוֹן is singular. Mosiah also sets off "like sheep" with commas.
7: Mosiah reads "so he opened not his mouth" where KJV reads "so he openeth not his mouth." Punctuation also differs (a semicolon for a colon, and no comma after "dumb").
8: Mosiah reads "the transgressions of my people" where KJV reads "the transgression of my people." The Hebrew פֶּשַׁע is singular. Punctuation also differs (semicolons for colons).
9: Mosiah reads "he had done no evil" where KJV reads "he had done no violence." The Hebrew חָמָס means violence or wrong.
10: Only punctuation differs: Mosiah has a semicolon where KJV has a colon after "grief," and no comma after "sin."
11: Mosiah reads "He shall see the travail of his soul" where KJV reads "He shall see of the travail of his soul." Punctuation also differs (a semicolon for a colon).
12: Mosiah reads "he bore the sins of many" where KJV reads "he bare the sin of many." The Hebrew חֵטְא is singular. Punctuation also differs (a semicolon for a colon).
